_comment: Captured surface of the CircleCI MCP server at https://mcp.circleci.com/mcp as of 2026-04-30. Hosted-bearer-PAT pattern (no OAuth, Personal API Token auth). The drift-check recipe lets an outsider validate tool naming and count without spinning up a live test harness.

token_capture_observed.token_visibility: shown once on creation, not retrievable later

self_hosted_branch.circleci_server: Set CIRCLECI_BASE_URL to your CircleCI Server host. The MCP server bundles the rest. Not currently tested by this SKILL.

drift_check_recipe.step_1: From any shell with curl + a CircleCI PAT in $CIRCLECI_TOKEN: curl -s -H "Circle-Token: $CIRCLECI_TOKEN" https://circleci.com/api/v2/me | jq '.'
drift_check_recipe.step_2: Confirm the API responds 200 and your PAT is valid. If the response shape drifts (new top-level fields, removed fields), the MCP server is likely also updated.
drift_check_recipe.step_3: Compare the canonical tool list in tool_surface_observed.examples against the live MCP tool surface inside Claude Code. Any new tool needs a SKILL Prompt-to-Tool Mapping row. Any removed tool needs a SKILL update.

_why_no_automated_script: Drift checking on a third-party SaaS is rate-limit-aware work and PAT-bearing. CI cannot safely run it without exposing the token. The recipe above runs from a human-driven shell when drift is suspected.
